test_title: PYST 39 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

The child said that he was afraid of the dark and requested the lady to stay with him.

options.text: The child said, "I am afraid of the dark. Please stay with me."
The child said, "I was afraid of the dark. Kindly stay with me."
The child said, "I am afraid of the dark. Will you stay with me?"
The child said, "I was afraid of the dark. Stay with me."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The child said that he was afraid of the dark and requested the lady to stay with him.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"he was afraid of the dark" becomes "I am afraid of the dark"**:
 
 
• The pronoun "he" changes to "I" because the child is speaking in direct speech.
 
• The verb "was" is changed to "am" to reflect the present tense in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **"requested the lady to stay with him" becomes "Please stay with me"**:
 
 
• The polite request in indirect speech is transformed into a direct request using "Please."
 
• The pronoun "him" is replaced with "me" to align with the speaker's point of view in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• The first letter of the sentence starts with a capital letter, and the sentence ends with a period or appropriate punctuation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The child said, "I am afraid of the dark. Please stay with me.""*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "I was afraid of the dark. Kindly stay with me."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "was" implies past tense, which does not align with the context of the child's current fear.
 
• "Kindly" is less commonly used in such contexts compared to "Please."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "I am afraid of the dark. Will you stay with me?"
 
 
• Incorrect request format: "Will you stay with me?" changes the polite request into a question, altering the intended tone.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "I was afraid of the dark. Stay with me."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "was" implies past tense, which does not match the current context of fear.
 
• The tone of "Stay with me" is more commanding than a polite request.
